title: U.S. House · New York's 23rd District
area: Western New York, including Chautauqua, Cattaraugus, Allegany, Wyoming, Livingston, Ontario, Yates, Steuben, Schuyler and part of Erie County.

context.text: Aaron Gies defeated Kevin Stocker in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 70.7%-27.9%. The Republican and Conservative primaries were canceled; incumbent Nick Langworthy advanced without appearing on either ballot.

summary.text: Nick Langworthy is the Republican and Conservative incumbent, a Western New York native who worked as a congressional district-office staffer and founded a polling firm before chairing the Erie County Republican Committee and then the New York Republican State Committee. First elected to the House in 2022, he serves on the Energy and Commerce, Oversight and Government Reform and Rules committees and chairs the Rules Committee's Legislative and Budget Process Subcommittee. His office says his work is focused on constituent service, jobs and economic opportunity for Western New York and the Southern Tier, and protecting constitutional rights.

background.text: Born in Jamestown, New York, and attended Pine Valley Central School; according to his congressional office, his upbringing included working in his family's bar and restaurant business.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from Niagara University in 2003.
Began his career in the district office of former Rep. Tom Reynolds and later served as district office director for Rep. Chris Lee; also founded and ran the polling firm Liberty Opinion Research.
Became chairman of the Erie County Republican Committee in 2010 and chairman of the New York Republican State Committee in 2019, serving in the state role until his election to Congress.
Was elected to represent New York's 23rd District in 2022 and took office in 2023, succeeding Rep. Joe Sempolinski.

Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee (Health, Energy and Environment subcommittees), the Oversight and Government Reform Committee and the Rules Committee, where he is chairman of the Legislative and Budget Process Subcommittee in the 119th Congress.

According to his office, he was a leader during House consideration of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 on airline safety measures adopted after the Colgan Air Flight 3407 crash in Clarence, New York.
Co-chairs the Maple Caucus and belongs to the Northern Border Security Caucus and the Rural Health Caucus, among other congressional caucuses.
His office states that he and his wife, Erin, live in Pendleton, New York, with their son and daughter.

priorities.text: Describes his focus as protecting constitutional rights and what his campaign materials call the values that make America a strong and prosperous country.

positions.summary: In a June 2025 press release, he says state and local governments must comply with federal immigration enforcement, that he stands with ICE officers, and that his bill would withhold federal funds from jurisdictions that do not cooperate.
positions.quote: State and local governments MUST comply with federal immigration enforcement efforts, and if they don’t, the Stop Dangerous Sanctuary Cities Act would withhold federal financial assistance from them. We must stand with our heroic ICE officers, our men and women in blue, and with the American people who cry out for safety and common sense in their local governments.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the Committee on Energy and Commerce (Health, Energy and Environment subcommittees), and chairs the Legislative and Budget Process Subcommittee of the Committee on Rules in the 119th Congress.

summary.text: Aaron Gies is a theology professor at St. Bonaventure University who won the Democratic nomination in June 2026 and is also the Working Families Party nominee; Spectrum News described him as a political newcomer. A scholar of medieval Franciscan theology, he describes his earlier work as including teaching, nonprofit leadership, waiting tables, bookkeeping and farm work. He is challenging incumbent Rep. Nick Langworthy on a message that a good life should be affordable, with priorities including universal healthcare, housing and public schools.

background.text: Gies says he was raised in a working family; his father ran a small contracting business and his mother worked as a school secretary.
background.quote: I was raised in a working family. My father ran a small contracting business. My mother worked as a school secretary.

background.text: Holds a B.A. in Bible and Religion from Montreat College (2002), an M.A. in Christian Thought from Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (2007), an M.A. in Medieval Studies (2010) and a Ph.D. in Historical and Systematic Theology (2018) from The Catholic University of America, and a 2023 diploma in manuscript studies from the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies.
Describes his career before academia as including work as a teacher and nonprofit leader, waiting tables, balancing books for a Main Street business and working on a nonprofit farm.
background.quote: I've spent my life serving communities — as a teacher, nonprofit leader, and person of faith.

background.text: Joined St. Bonaventure University in 2019 as a research postdoctoral fellow, became a regular member of the Department of Theology and Franciscan Studies in 2021, and is now an associate professor.
Is Associate Editor of the Franciscan Institute's journal Franciscan Studies and has published translations of the medieval theologian Alexander of Hales.
The university's faculty profile says he serves as a cantor in his parish and helps at his wife's veterinary clinic.
Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Erie County attorney Kevin Stocker; Spectrum News described him as a political newcomer.

priorities.text: Says his central campaign message is that a good life should be affordable, citing rising costs, wages that have not kept pace, and corporations getting special treatment.
priorities.quote: A good life should not be a luxury.

priorities.text: Cites medical debt as one of the most common causes of bankruptcy and says cuts to Medicare, Medicaid, VA benefits, and rural healthcare systems threaten local hospitals and nursing homes.
priorities.quote: Medical debt is now one of the most common causes of bankruptcy in America.

priorities.text: Says he would strengthen unions and workers' bargaining power rather than give tax breaks and deregulation to large corporations.
priorities.quote: Instead of tax breaks and deregulation for large corporations, Aaron supports raising wages and strengthening workers' bargaining power.

priorities.text: Describes housing as scarce and increasingly unaffordable in Western New York and the Southern Tier and says it should be treated as a basic human need rather than only an investment.
priorities.quote: Housing is not just an investment; it is a basic human need.

positions.summary: Supports codifying Roe v. Wade's abortion protections into federal law and would oppose a national abortion ban.
positions.quote: I support codifying the protections of Roe into law and would vote no on any attempted national abortion ban.

positions.summary: Supports universal background checks and red-flag laws while also affirming Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: I support universal background checks and red flag laws to keep guns out of the hands of those who are likely to use them to commit crimes.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he supports building a universal healthcare system that guarantees basic care for every American.
positions.quote: Aaron supports building a universal healthcare system that guarantees stable, accessible, cost‑effective basic care for every American.

positions.summary: Supports renewable energy development and opposes new fracking and nuclear projects.
positions.quote: Renewable energy makes us more resilient and energy independent and I'll fight for federal dollars for these projects, but also make sure local concerns are heard and local people benefit directly. I oppose irresponsible data center buildout, fracking and new nuclear projects.

positions.summary: Campaign site lists raising the federal minimum wage to $15 immediately among the actions he will fight for.
positions.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage to $15 immediately.

researchNotes: Gies's biography draws on his campaign website's Meet Aaron section, his St. Bonaventure faculty profile and Spectrum News. His Ballotpedia page still has no biography section and no completed Candidate Connection survey. A fact-check found that two claims sourced to the site could not be verified there: a "$15 minimum wage" quote (no mention of minimum wage or $15 anywhere on the site) and an "Expand housing supply to drive down costs" quote (the housing section only frames housing as unaffordable and a basic human need, with no supply/zoning-specific commitment); the `minimum_wage` and `housing_supply` positions built on those quotes were removed, and the housing priority and healthcare quotes were corrected to text actually on the page. Federal key votes and FEC totals for incumbent Nick Langworthy are added separately by script. Gies's campaign site gives no birthplace, hometown or year of birth and his Ballotpedia page has no biography, so those details are not included; Langworthy's official bio does not list a year of birth.
